descriptors.definition: Government entities provide monetary or non-monetary grants and assistance to entities for industrial, geographic, and social development purposes. Ind AS 20 governs the appropriate accounting treatment and disclosures required for these transactions.
inclusion: Disclosure of other forms of government assistance
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from general government assistance like infrastructure provision available to the entire community.

descriptors.concept_name: Scope of Government Grants and Assistance
descriptors.definition: The standard applies specifically to the accounting and disclosure of government grants and other forms of government assistance. It sets boundaries by excluding tax-related benefits, ownership participations, and agricultural grants.
exclusion: Tax benefits like investment tax credits
nearby_distinctions: Excludes general infrastructural benefits not specific to qualifying entities.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 20 mandates the specific accounting methods and disclosure norms for government grants received by entities. It also governs the required disclosures for general forms of government assistance.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on direct entity-specific transfers rather than broad macroeconomic fiscal policies.

descriptors.definition: Certain items are excluded from the purview of Ind AS 20, including tax-related benefits, price-level adjustments, and government ownership stakes. These exclusions ensure specialized standards or tax laws govern those specific transactions instead.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between specific economic grants and general taxation benefits or equity investments.

descriptors.definition: Government assistance involves actions supplying specific economic benefits to qualifying entities, excluding broad community infrastructure or normal trading transactions. It requires careful evaluation when resources are transferred to appropriately reflect financial statement impact.
nearby_distinctions: General trading activities with government cannot be arbitrarily segregated as assistance.

descriptors.definition: Government grants are recognized only when there is reasonable assurance that the entity will comply with attached conditions and that the grant will be received. Mere physical receipt of funds does not automatically constitute conclusive evidence of condition fulfillment.
exclusion: Grants without reasonable assurance of compliance or receipt
nearby_distinctions: Differs from cash-basis recognition by requiring the dual threshold of condition compliance assurance and receipt likelihood.

descriptors.definition: Forgivable loans from governments convert to grants when there is reasonable assurance the entity will satisfy forgiveness terms. Below-market interest rate loans derive a government grant component measured as the difference between initial fair value under financial instrument standards and proceeds received.
exclusion: Standard commercial loans at prevailing market rates
nearby_distinctions: Below-market loans split into a financial liability measured at fair value and a deferred grant benefit.

descriptors.concept_name: Accounting for Loans at Less Than Market Rate
descriptors.definition: The benefit derived from a government loan carrying a below-market interest rate is treated as a government grant. This benefit equals the difference between the initial carrying value determined via financial instrument standards and the actual proceeds received.
inclusion: Initial fair value measurement of loan
Amortization of grant benefit over expense periods
exclusion: Market-rate loans lacking any government subsidy element
nearby_distinctions: Requires present value discounting using market interest rates rather than nominal loan rates.

descriptors.concept_name: Accrual Versus Receipts Basis and Specific Grant Types
descriptors.definition: Recognizing government grants on a receipts basis violates accrual accounting principles unless no other allocation method exists. Grants compensating for past expenses or providing immediate financial support are recognized in profit or loss during the period they become receivable.
exclusion: Arbitrary cash-basis recognition when systematic allocation is feasible
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts systematic deferral models by immediately expensing or recognizing grants lacking future matching costs.

descriptors.concept_name: Grants Related to Non-Depreciable Assets and Non-Monetary Transfers
descriptors.definition: Grants tied to non-depreciable assets requiring specific fulfillment obligations are recognized over the periods bearing those compliance costs. Non-monetary asset transfers are recorded at either assessed fair value or nominal value alongside the corresponding grant.
inclusion: Transfer of resources for entity use
exclusion: Standard depreciable asset grants mapped directly to depreciation lives
nearby_distinctions: Non-depreciable asset grants link to obligation fulfillment periods rather than asset depreciation schedules.

descriptors.definition: Grants received within complex financial or fiscal aid packages require identifying specific underlying cost conditions to determine appropriate revenue recognition periods. Non-monetary grants under these packages can alternatively be recognized at full fair value or nominal amounts.
nearby_distinctions: Demands splitting multi-faceted aid packages across varying expense-matching timelines.

descriptors.concept_name: Grants for Past Expenses and Non-Monetary Valuations
descriptors.definition: Grants acting as compensation for past expenses or immediate financial support without future cost obligations are recognized directly in profit or loss when receivable. Non-monetary asset transfers are measured at fair value or nominal value with equivalent deferred income setup.
inclusion: Fair value or nominal asset recording
exclusion: Grants tied to future expenditure obligations
nearby_distinctions: Immediate recognition applies when no further performance obligations or future costs remain.
